title: Frobenius-equivariant rational finite-fibre base change
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $g_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a finite etale morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g=g_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart]. Use the rational/common-stage direct image $Rg_*$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The object $Rg_*\mathcal F$ is concentrated in degree zero, and its degree-zero sheaf $g_*\mathcal F$ is constructible with the Weil structure induced by direct image of that of $\mathcal F$.

Let $y$ be a closed point of $Y_0$, write $L=\kappa(y)$ and $d_y=[L:k_0]$ [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], choose a $k_0$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow k$, and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ be its geometric lift. Put $Z_0=X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $Z=Z_0\times_L k$. Then $Z_0$ is finite over $L$, and restriction of $\mathcal F$ to $Z$ defines a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal G$ on the $L$-scheme $Z_0$: its Weil structure uses the degree-$d_y$ iterate of the structure on $\mathcal F$ and the canonical geometric-point reparametrization. Here local and global geometric Frobenius use [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. The finite-fibre base-change map is a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$b_y:(g_*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G),$$
with geometric compact cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and it satisfies
$$b_y F_y=F_{Z/L} b_y,$$
where $F_{Z/L}$ is geometric Frobenius relative to the finite field $L$ on $H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$. These stalks and operators are interpreted at a common finite coefficient-field stage and extended to $\Qlb$.

Closed points $z_0$ of $Z_0$ correspond bijectively to the points $x$ of $X_0$ above $y$; those $x$ are closed, and $\kappa(z_0)=\kappa(x)$ as extensions of $L$. For every geometric lift of $z_0$, the restriction map identifies the stalk of $\mathcal G$ with the stalk of $\mathcal F$ at the corresponding lift of $x$, and carries its local geometric-Frobenius operator relative to $L$ to the original $F_x$ relative to $k_0$. No purity, lissity, semisimplicity or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First work at finite coefficients $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. A finite etale map is etale-locally a finite disjoint union of identity maps, including the empty union [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split]. On such a neighborhood its pro-etale direct image is the finite product of the restrictions to the sheets: evaluation on $T\to U$ gives the product of sections on the copies of $T$. Restriction to these etale neighborhoods is exact and preserves injectives [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], so the same calculation computes the derived image of a bounded complex. Thus it is exact and preserves its cohomological interval. The finite products commute with derived change $A_m\to A_n$ (finite products are finite sums, and tensor is additive); consequently the canonical coefficient-exchange maps for this direct image are isomorphisms. These identities glue, since their maps are the restriction and coefficient maps themselves. For constructibility, represent a finite-level constructible pro-etale complex by its etale antecedent [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The sheaf comparison $\nu_Y^*g_*\to g_*\nu_X^*$ is the identity on every sheet in the preceding calculation, hence is an isomorphism. The etale direct image is exact and constructible by [fin4-thm-finite-morphisms-constructible]. This proves finite-level constructibility on $Y$ without assuming $X$ or $Y$ separated.

source.place: Tag 04HN, lemma-finite-etale-etale-local; finite-level constructibility supplied by the cited existing fin4 theorem.

proof.text: Let $K$ be an integral constructible complex representing an object at coefficient field $E$. Its reductions $K_n$ are constructible in a single interval $[a,b]$, by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. By Step 1 the tower $M_n=Rg_*K_n$ is constructible in that same interval, and its canonical quotient comparisons $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ are isomorphisms. Apply the direct image to the strict coefficient tower representing $K$; this supplies the coherent tower and quotient cocycle, not merely an inverse system in a homotopy category. Thus it is a normalized tower in the sense of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. The effectivity theorem [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] identifies every reduction of $M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$ with $M_n$ and makes $M$ derived complete. Together with the already proved constructibility and uniform interval this is exactly membership in the integral category. This $M$ is the integral $Rg_*K$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Localizing scalars therefore gives $Rg_*$ on the required rational constructible category. No finite-Tor bound on the reductions was used.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $U_{i,0}$ of $Y_0$ and put $U_i=U_{i,0}\times_{k_0}k$: these are affine opens covering $Y$, stable under the base-field Frobenius $\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. Their inverse images $V_i$ are affine since $g$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]; these are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Finite-level open restriction commutes with derived image [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction]. It also commutes with the derived limit defining the integral image: ringed-site open restriction is exact with exact left adjoint extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], hence preserves injectives and limits, also on towers. Completed restriction is the same restriction [lem-sf-pf-open-factor-coherence](1). These comparisons pass to rational localization. Consequently $(Rg_*\mathcal F)|_{U_i}=R(g|_{V_i})_*(\mathcal F|_{V_i})$. Apply [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] to each $V_i\to U_i$: this lies in degree zero. This is a local assertion for the standard constructible t-structure [prop-constructible-truncations]; its sheaf interpretation and checking on separated open covers are [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact]. Explicitly, at an integral representative each cohomology sheaf outside degree zero is killed locally by a power of $\varpi_E$; a finite cover gives a single power, so it vanishes after rational localization. Hence $Rg_*\mathcal F$ is in the constructible heart. The same local finite-adic lemma supplies the canonical stalk-to-fibre-sections isomorphism, natural also for semilinear isomorphisms of diagrams. It is independent of the affine neighborhood because all its arrows are restriction maps.

proof.text: Write $\phi_X,\phi_Y$ for the geometric base-field Frobenius automorphisms, to distinguish them from $g$. The finite morphism $g_0$ is proper and in particular separated [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Steps 1--3 have verified the bounded-constructibility domain; therefore [lem-fix-weil-operations] applies. If $\theta:\phi_X^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is its Weil structure, the induced structure on the degree-zero image is $\phi_Y^*g_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}}g_*\phi_X^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{g_*\theta}g_*\mathcal F$. Its iterates use the iterated exchanges and $\theta^{[n]}$. The composition comparisons and exchanges are equivariant by the same cited lemma. This proves the claimed induced Weil structure, having established constructibility separately rather than inferring it from equivariance.

source.place: First paragraph: rational finite-stalk comparison; agent refinement of the coefficient and equivariance details.

proof.text: The field $L=\kappa(y)$ has finite degree $d_y$ over $k_0$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a). Base change of a finite morphism is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], so $Z_0$ is finite over $L$ and proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The map $Z_0\to X_0$ is the base change of the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y_0$, and hence is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. In an affine neighborhood of $y$, write $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and its finite inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Then $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(y))$. Prime ideals in this quotient correspond exactly to primes of $B$ over the maximal ideal of $y$. Their residue fields are unchanged, also as $L$-fields [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso]. Each is finite over $L$: the corresponding quotient of the finite-dimensional $L$-algebra is a finite-dimensional domain and hence a field, since multiplication by any nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective. Thus these $x$ are closed also in $X_0$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a). This proves the point correspondence and all residue-field assertions, without a surjectivity assumption.

source.place: Tag 03QP, finite-fibre setup; elementary affine fibre calculation spelling out the residue fields.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\to X$ be the fibre inclusion with the chosen embedding $L\hookrightarrow k$. The pullback $i^*\mathcal F$ is constructible: integral pullback preserves constructibility and reduces to ordinary inverse image [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](1). It lies in the constructible heart, because pullback along the morphism $i$ of finite-type $k$-schemes is $t$-exact and commutes with $\mathcal H^j$ [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact]. By the same lemma and pullback composition its geometric fibres are those of $\mathcal F$, which on the separated affine charts $V_i$ of Step 3 are the exact fibre functors of [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact]. Put $\psi_Z=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^{d_y})$, the base-field Frobenius for $L$. Since $\gamma^{d_y}$ fixes $L$, $i\psi_Z=\phi_X^{d_y}i$. Pull back $\theta^{[d_y]}$ along $i$ and use this equality to define $\eta:\psi_Z^*i^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*\mathcal F$. Iterates and reparametrizations are precisely those of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], with the associative pullback comparisons [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], localized at $E$. This gives the asserted Weil sheaf $\mathcal G=(i^*\mathcal F,\eta)$ on $Z_0/L$.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), printed pp.150--152: Frobenius and change of finite base field; agent construction with the specified pullback comparisons.

proof.text: Let $a_y:(g_*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ be the restriction isomorphism from Step 3 and [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image]. Since $Z_0/L$ is proper, [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius] gives a natural isomorphism $c:H_c^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ compatible with Frobenius transport. Define $b_y=c^{-1}a_y$. This is the usual finite-fibre base-change map followed by proper compact/ordinary identification. It remains to check its operator, rather than only its underlying vector space.

source.place: First paragraph: rational finite-stalk comparison; agent refinement of the coefficient and equivariance details.

proof.text: On the chart $V_i\to U_i$ of Step 3 containing $\bar y$, which $\phi_X,\phi_Y$ preserve, apply the semilinear diagram-naturality of [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] to $\phi_X^{d_y},\phi_Y^{d_y}$ and the point return $\phi_Y^{d_y}\bar y=\bar y\gamma_s^{d_y}$. It identifies the transport of the source of $a_y$ with cohomology transport along $\psi_Z$ on its target. Concretely every restriction to a geometric lift in the fibre is reindexed by $\phi_X^{d_y}$ and has the induced point transport; these are the same restrictions on both routes. Naturality for the sheaf morphism $\theta^{[d_y]}$ then identifies the subsequent source action with $H^0(\eta)$. The point-transport naturality identity [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) permits exactly these restriction and structure maps to pass through the transports. Thus the composite on the source is $F_y$ by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], whereas the target composite is ordinary $L$-Frobenius by [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. The transports used here are the specified isomorphisms [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso], applied with finite base $L$. Hence $a_yF_y=F_{Z/L}^{\mathrm{ord}}a_y$. Proper-coincidence transport compatibility [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius](2), followed by naturality for $\eta$, gives $cF_{Z/L}=F_{Z/L}^{\mathrm{ord}}c$. Combining the two equalities proves $b_yF_y=F_{Z/L}b_y$.

proof.text: For a point $z_0$ corresponding to $x$ put $e=[\kappa(x):L]$. Step 5 identifies the fields, and the elementary tower formula gives $[\kappa(x):k_0]=ed_y$. At a chosen geometric lift, pullback composition identifies the stalk of $\mathcal G$ with that of $\mathcal F$. In the formula [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] for its local operator over $L$, the structure map is the $e$-fold iterate of $\eta$. Expanding $\eta$ gives the same ordered string of $ed_y$ factors $\theta$ as $\theta^{[ed_y]}$. The point transport is likewise the ordered string of $ed_y$ one-step transports, grouped into $e$ blocks of length $d_y$; the point reparametrization is $\gamma_s^{ed_y}$ in either expression. Associativity of the specified pullback comparisons [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] removes the parentheses, and naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] identifies the intervening pullback maps. The two composites are therefore identical, which proves that the relative-$L$ local operator is the original $F_x$. This checks the operator itself, with its geometric-Frobenius convention, rather than merely its trace or eigenvalues.

source.place: (1.1.8)--(1.1.10), printed pp.150--152; agent expansion of the iterates.

proof.text: For $\Qlb$ choose a common finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ representing $\mathcal F$, its Weil isomorphism and inverse, and their inverse identities. Such a stage exists by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. All constructions above commute with enlarging this field: for the stalk formula this is part of [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image], and for point transports it is part of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2). All other arrows are canonical coefficient-stage pullbacks, direct images and their comparisons already constructed at that stage. Extend the equalities to $\Qlb$. Empty fibres give zero on both sides; degree-one points give the one-step action; disconnected fibres require no choice of ordering. Nothing in the argument uses purity, lissity or semisimplicity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q127-e10b22735 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its parent lem-a1-finite-map-purity (main-20261015, proof first paragraph), all 28 dependency statements, Stacks 03QP/04HN and Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.10-6.8.15. The statement is true and not weakened. It keeps non-separated X0/Y0 and the rational/common-stage coefficients, and its base-change map is fibre restriction from lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image followed by the inverse of the proper coincidence. I checked Z = X x_Y ybar, the identity i psi_Z = phi_X^{d_y} i, e*d_y = [kappa(x):k0], and the small cases id, Spec F_{q^2}->Spec F_q and the empty fibre. Two faults, both repaired. (1) E1/E5: Step 8 uses lem-zl's semilinear naturality under phi^{d_y}, which needs a Frobenius-stable chart, but Step 3 took an arbitrary affine cover of Y. Steps 3 and 8 now use U_{i,0} x_{k0} k from an affine cover of Y0. (2) C1/C4: Step 6 put i^*F in the heart using fibre functors that lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact gives only on the heart; this needs t-exactness of pullback, and no node stated it.
